faqs.q: How much will it cost to get wildlife out of my Pineville home?
faqs.a: It depends on the job — a single squirrel entry sealed early is very different work from a raccoon family in a chimney or a bat colony in the attic. We inspect first and provide a straightforward quote after inspection, so you know the full scope before any work starts.

faqs.q: What is thumping in my Pineville attic at dusk?
faqs.a: Heavy dusk thumping usually means a raccoon — in spring, often a mother denning with pups in the attic or chimney. We check for a litter first, remove the family, and seal the entry in steel with a proper cap.

faqs.q: What should I expect to pay for wildlife removal in Mullens?
faqs.a: Cost turns on the animal, where it has gotten in, and how much proofing the building needs afterward. Our crew walks the property, shows you the entry points, and gives you a quote after inspection before work begins.

faqs.q: Why do snakes turn up around Mullens stone walls and woodpiles?
faqs.a: Rock walls and woodpiles shelter mice, and snakes — mostly harmless rat snakes, copperheads on rocky ground — follow the food. It is illegal to kill any snake in the wild in West Virginia; our crew captures problem snakes non-lethally and liberates them at the site of capture.
